q: If the atoms in a covalent bond are not identical, the electrons will not be equally shared, resulting in bond _____.
e: If the atoms in a covalent bond are not identical, the electrons will not be equally shared, resulting in bond polarity. A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between atoms.

q: The atom with the greater share of the electrons will be slightly negative and the other atom will be slightly positive, known as a _____.
e: The atom with the greater share of the electrons will be slightly negative and the other atom will be slightly positive, known as a dipole. A dipole is a plus end and a minus end separated in space.

q: Depending on the difference in electronegativity, covalent bonds can be polar or _____.
e: Depending on the difference in electronegativity, covalent bonds can be polar or non-polar. Electronegativity measures how strongly an atom pulls shared bonding electrons toward itself.

q: The bond becomes more polar as the difference in electronegativity values of the atoms in a covalent bond _____.
e: The bond becomes more polar as the difference in electronegativity values of the atoms in a covalent bond increases. Electronegativity measures how strongly an atom pulls shared bonding electrons toward itself.

q: In a covalent bond formed between two similar non-metal atoms, the shared electron pair is equally attracted resulting in a _____ covalent bond.
e: In a covalent bond formed between two similar non-metal atoms, the shared electron pair is equally attracted resulting in a non-polar covalent bond. A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between atoms.

q: The degree of bond polarity is measured as a _____ of a bond.
e: The degree of bond polarity is measured as a dipole moment of a bond. Dipole moment measures how polar a bond or molecule is.

q: Any non-polar covalent bond has a _____ dipole moment.
e: Any non-polar covalent bond has a zero dipole moment. In a non-polar covalent bond the two atoms share the electron pair evenly.

q: In the case of polyatomic molecules, the dipole moment of a molecule is the _____ sum of the dipole moments of various bonds.
e: In the case of polyatomic molecules, the dipole moment of a molecule is the vector sum of the dipole moments of various bonds. Dipole moment measures how polar a bond or molecule is.

q: The $H_2O$ molecule has a bent shape and the total dipole moment is not zero, so it is a _____ molecule.
e: The H2O molecule has a bent shape and the total dipole moment is not zero, so it is a polar molecule. Dipole moment measures how polar a bond or molecule is.

q: In the $CO_2$ molecule, the two equal bond dipoles point in opposite directions and cancel the effect of each other, thus it is a _____ molecule.
e: In the CO2 molecule, the two equal bond dipoles point in opposite directions and cancel the effect of each other, thus it is a non-polar molecule. A dipole is a plus end and a minus end separated in space.

q: Van der Waals forces are weak forces which include dipole-dipole interaction, ion-dipole interaction, and _____ forces.
e: Van der Waals forces are weak forces which include dipole-dipole interaction, ion-dipole interaction, and London dispersion forces. London dispersion forces are weak temporary-dipole attractions found in every substance.

q: Dipole-dipole interactions are formed when two _____ molecules interact with each other in space.
e: Dipole-dipole interactions are formed when two dipolar molecules interact with each other in space. Dipole-dipole attraction lines up the positive end of one polar molecule with the negative end of another.

q: Ion-dipole interaction is formed from the interaction between an ion and a _____ molecule.
e: Ion-dipole interaction is formed from the interaction between an ion and a dipole molecule. Ion-dipole attraction is the pull between an ion and the charged end of a polar molecule.

q: The weakest intermolecular forces that can be formed between atoms as well as non-polar molecules are known as _____ forces.
e: The weakest intermolecular forces that can be formed between atoms as well as non-polar molecules are known as London dispersion forces. London dispersion forces are weak temporary-dipole attractions found in every substance.

q: Because of the constant motion of the electrons, an atom can develop a _____ dipole when the electrons are distributed unsymmetrically.
e: Because of the constant motion of the electrons, an atom can develop a temporary dipole when the electrons are distributed unsymmetrically. A dipole is a plus end and a minus end separated in space.

q: London dispersion forces are also called induced dipole-_____ interaction.
e: London dispersion forces are also called induced dipole-induced dipole interaction. London dispersion forces are weak temporary-dipole attractions found in every substance.

q: Due to London dispersion forces, non-polar substances can condense into liquids and can freeze into solids when the temperature is lowered, such as liquid nitrogen and dry ice which is solid _____.
e: Due to London dispersion forces, non-polar substances can condense into liquids and can freeze into solids when the temperature is lowered, such as liquid nitrogen and dry ice which is solid CO2. London dispersion forces are weak temporary-dipole attractions found in every substance.

q: The formation of hydrogen bonds requires the first molecule to have hydrogen attached to a high electronegative atom such as F, O, or _____.
e: The formation of hydrogen bonds requires the first molecule to have hydrogen attached to a high electronegative atom such as F, O, or N. A hydrogen bond is the strong intermolecular pull from H attached to N, O, or F toward another N, O, or F.

q: A hydrogen bond is a special type of dipole-dipole interaction and is the _____ of all intermolecular forces.
e: A hydrogen bond is a special type of dipole-dipole interaction and is the strongest of all intermolecular forces. Intermolecular forces tug neighbouring molecules or ions together; they are not the bonds inside a molecule.
